title: What If You Could See the Dreams Your Parents Gave Up for You?

facts.claim: 76% of people said their single biggest regret was failing to become their ideal self
facts.source: Davidai & Gilovich (2018), 'The ideal road not taken', Emotion; Cornell Chronicle

facts.claim: Vera Wang was a figure skater and journalist and entered fashion design at 40
Private pilot training costs about $6,000 to $20,000+
facts.source: AOPA, 'How much does a pilot's license cost?'

facts.claim: Raising a child to 17 costs about $310,605 (middle-income family, born 2015)
facts.source: Brookings Institution for the Wall Street Journal (2022)

facts.claim: Parents' sleep does not fully recover for up to 6 years after their first child
There is no maximum age for a US private pilot certificate
facts.source: FAA rules as summarised by AOPA and flight schools (minimum 17, medical required)

lines.text: There's a ghost behind your mom. The pilot she never became.
You have 30 days before she loses it. But nobody knows why your dad's is invisible.
Sweetie, you're staring. Is there something on my face?
No! You look... great.
By the end of the month, you'll make 15,000 dollars, turn your whole school upside down, and find out the one dream in your house you got completely wrong.
Here's how it works. Behind every grown-up floats the person they almost became.
Bright means they're still close. Faint means they've almost given up. And when it fades out completely, it's gone. Forever.
Kids don't have one yet. It shows up the day you turn 18.
That's real, by the way. In a 2018 Cornell study, 76 percent of people said their biggest regret was not becoming who they wanted to be.
Your mom's ghost is almost see-through.
And Mom has no idea. She's been carrying it around for 17 years.
Why is our kid staring at your head?
I think it's a phase.
The next morning, the whole world is haunted.
Sit down. Don't touch anything. Don't talk to me.
Behind him, a ghost in a tuxedo is singing opera.
The businessman in row 3? His ghost is a surfer. The toddler in row 5 has no ghost. Just snacks.
Phones away. Today is the most exciting day of the year. Fractions.
Your math teacher's ghost is a stuntman. On fire. On a motorcycle.
The principal's ghost is a DJ. The gym coach's ghost is a ballet dancer. He's very good.
Twenty laps! Nobody cares about your feelings!
Behind him, a perfect pirouette.
And the lunch lady's ghost is a fashion designer in Paris.
Real fact: Vera Wang was a figure skater and a journalist. She didn't design her first dress until she was 40.
Okay, okay. What's my ghost?
You're 17. You don't have one yet.
Then make one up!
That night at dinner, a plane flies over the house.
Boeing 737. Running late.
She does that. Every plane, every time.
Nobody ever asked her why.
And your dad's ghost? You can barely see it at all. Like it's standing in exactly the same spot he is.
You figure his dream must be almost gone.
You do the math. Mom's ghost loses a little light every day. 30 days.
Flight school costs anywhere from 6,000 to 20,000 dollars. That's real.
You have 43 dollars and a library card.
So you start a business. Dream Detective. 20 dollars, and you tell people who they almost became.
Seriously? A stand-up comedian? Me?
She does an open mic that night. She kills.
Not every ghost is a surprise, though. The mailman's ghost is... a mailman. Same bag. Same shorts.
Huh. Guess I already got it.
Remember that guy. He matters later.
Your math teacher jumps a motorcycle over the school fountain at the pep rally. The fire alarm is not a fan.
And the bus driver sings opera on route 9. The video gets 6 million views.
By day 20, there's a line around the block.
Our kid is running a ghost business out of the garage. Should I be worried or proud?
Proud. The kid charges tax.
Day 5, 400 dollars. Day 12, 3,000. Day 20, 9,500 dollars.
Okay, what's my ghost now?
Still nothing, Theo.
Is it a Navy SEAL? It's a Navy SEAL.
But there's a cost. Once you can see everyone's dream, you start to notice whose dream you are.
Mom was accepted to flight school the year you were born. She never went.
You find the letter in the attic. Still in the envelope. Next to her old aviator jacket.
Raising one kid costs about 310,000 dollars. That's real. You weren't the reason she didn't go. You were the price.
Oh, and parents' sleep doesn't fully recover for 6 years after their first kid. You owe her a lot of naps.
And somewhere in all of this, you get an email of your own. The summer animation program you applied to. Accepted.
Deposit: 14,800 dollars. Due day 30. Same day as flight school.
So you tell her. All of it.
Sweetie, I'm 47. That plane has left.
lines.act: gentle, a little sad, trying to smile

lines.text: She's not wrong. It's a big plane.
But here's the thing. There's no maximum age for a private pilot license in America. None.
Grandma Moses didn't start painting until she was 78.
Her ghost flickers. Just a little.
Day 28. You wake up and her ghost is gone. Completely gone.
Then it flickers back. Fainter than ever. Two days left.
Day 30. 4:59 p.m. You have 15,000 dollars.
Two deadlines. One minute. Your deposit, or her flight school.
Bro! 30 seconds! Click something!
Your animation program. The thing you've wanted since you were 6.
On one screen, your future. On the other, hers. 10 seconds.
Your finger is on the button. And behind you, in the window, something faint appears. Your own ghost.
You press the other one.
Three weeks later, a small plane flies over your house.
Earlier that morning, her instructor told her most people are nervous on their first flight.
I've been ready for 17 years.
Cessna 172. Mine.
And her ghost catches up with her. Then it's gone. Because it doesn't have to float behind her anymore.
And Dad's ghost? The one you could barely see?
It was never fading. It was standing exactly where he is. Like the mailman's. Because the life your dad dreamed about is the one he's living.
I always wanted to be your dad. Your mom wanted to fly. Now we both get to.
Also, I called the animation school. Your deposit's paid. I've been saving since you were 6.
And sweetie? You were never the price. You were the point.
Okay. Now you have to tell me. What's my ghost?
Theo turned 18 last week. You look.
It's Theo. In sequins. Dancing.
And honestly? He's amazing.
It's a Navy SEAL.
I knew it!
Mom flies every Sunday now. She still names every plane she passes. Out loud. On the radio.
Air traffic control has asked her to stop.
That night, you look in the mirror. The faint shape from the window is back. Bright. Brand new.
And it winks.
So if you could see the dream your parents gave up for you, would you want to know? Tell us in the comments.
